dashboard.title: Overview
dashboard.apiHint: Make sure rustcache is running and the API is available on 127.0.0.1:8080.

exclusions.title: Exclusions
exclusions.description: Requests to the listed domains and networks are <1>not cached</1> and <2>do not go through MITM</2> — the connection goes straight to the origin.

cache.title: Cache
cache.clearDesc: A full purge deletes all cached responses from disk. Cache keys are not recoverable — objects will be re-fetched from the origin.
cache.purgeConfirm: Delete all cache entries? This cannot be undone.

settings.title: Settings
settings.intro: Every config.toml key is editable here. Changes are written back and applied live where possible. Ports, paths and bind addresses take effect after a restart.
settings.httpProxyHint: Caching HTTP proxy port. Port changes need a restart.
settings.httpsMitmHint: HTTPS interception port (requires CA). Port changes need a restart.
settings.socks5Hint: SOCKS5 tunnel port (no caching). Port changes need a restart.
settings.apiBindHint: REST API and web UI address, e.g. 127.0.0.1:8080.
settings.pathsModel: There is a single root — data_dir. Cache, CA and log paths default to sub-paths under it (e.g. "cache" → $data_dir/cache).
settings.dataDirHint: The one root data directory. CLI --data-dir overrides it for the process.
settings.cacheDirHint: Default "cache". Relative paths resolve under data_dir.
settings.caDirHint: Default "ca". Relative paths resolve under data_dir.
settings.logDbHint: Default "logs.db". Relative paths resolve under data_dir.
settings.pathsHint: Relative paths resolve under data_dir. Absolute paths (or ~/...) are used as-is and ignore data_dir. Changing directories requires a restart.
settings.maxSizeHint: On-disk cache size cap. Applied immediately.
settings.maxObjectHint: Largest response body eligible for caching. Applied immediately.
settings.pacEnabledHint: LAN listener serving proxy.pac / wpad.dat. Restart required.
settings.pacModeHint: What the PAC script advertises. Applied immediately.
settings.hotReloadDesc: Re-read config.toml and apply exclusion and cache-limit changes without a restart. Ports, paths and binds need a process restart.
settings.actionsDesc: Save writes the full configuration to config.toml and does not restart the process. The Restart button restarts it separately. Exclusions are edited on their own page.
settings.applyHotTitle: Applied on save, no restart needed
settings.applyRestartTitle: Takes effect only after a process restart
settings.applyLegend: Field badge: «hot» applies immediately, «restart» needs a process restart.
settings.restartConfirm: Restart the process? Listeners will drop briefly. Unsaved form changes will be lost.

connect.title: Connect
connect.intro: The proxy listens on 0.0.0.0 — connect from other devices via a LAN address. The API and this panel are only available on 127.0.0.1. Click an IP card — that address will be used in the instructions below.
connect.pacUrlLabel: PAC script URL for the selected address (mode: {{mode}}):
connect.pacWin: Settings → Network & internet → Proxy → «Automatic proxy setup» → «Use setup script» → paste the URL above.
connect.pacLinux: Settings → Network → «Network Proxy» → «Automatic proxy configuration URL» → paste the URL.
connect.pacMac: System Settings → Network → Wi-Fi/Ethernet → «Details…» → Proxies → «Automatic proxy configuration» → paste the URL above.
connect.pacIos: Settings → Wi-Fi → «i» on the network → «Configure Proxy» → «Automatic» → paste the URL above.
connect.pacAndroid: Wi-Fi → network → «Modify» → Advanced → Proxy: «Auto» / «Auto-config» (or «Proxy script») → PAC URL.
connect.pacExclusionsNote: Excluded hosts and CIDRs from the exclusion list get DIRECT (direct connection, no proxy). Environment variables http_proxy/https_proxy are not PAC: PAC operates at the browser/OS level.
connect.win1: Install the CA certificate (needed for HTTPS interception). Download <1>ca.crt</1>, then double-click → «Install Certificate» → «Local Machine» → «Trusted Root Certification Authorities».
connect.win2: System proxy: Settings → Network & internet → Proxy → «Use a proxy server» → address <1>{{ip}}</1>, port <2>{{port}}</2>.
connect.win5: SOCKS5 (tunnel without cache) — port <1>{{port}}</1>. In Firefox: Settings → Network → Manual proxy configuration → SOCKS Host <2>{{ip}}</2>, port <3>{{port}}</3>, SOCKS v5.
connect.lin1: Install the CA into the system trust store:
connect.lin3: GNOME: Settings → Network → Proxy → «Manual» → HTTP <1>{{http}}</1>, HTTPS <2>{{https}}</2>.
connect.mac1: Install the CA certificate (needed for HTTPS interception). Download <1>ca.crt</1>, then run in Terminal:
connect.mac2: System proxy: System Settings → Network → Wi-Fi (or Ethernet) → «Details…» → «Proxies» → «Web proxy (HTTP)» and «Secure web proxy (HTTPS)» → address <1>{{ip}}</1>, port <2>{{port}}</2>.
connect.mac3: Or from Terminal (replace «Wi-Fi» with your service name from networksetup -listallnetworkservices):
connect.mac5firefox: In Firefox: Settings → Network → Manual proxy configuration → SOCKS Host <1>{{ip}}</1>, port <2>{{port}}</2>, SOCKS v5.
connect.macNote: The macOS proxy applies system-wide to most apps. Individual apps can also use http_proxy/https_proxy or their own settings. Certificates with pinning will not work through MITM.
connect.ios1: Install the CA certificate: open <1>ca.crt</1> in Safari (or download the file) → «Allow» → «Install Profile». Then Settings → General → About → «Certificate Trust Settings» → enable full trust for the RustCache CA.
connect.ios2: Wi-Fi proxy: Settings → Wi-Fi → «i» on the connected network → «Configure Proxy» → «Manual» → Server: <1>{{ip}}</1>, Port: <2>{{port}}</2>.
connect.ios3: Or PAC: «Automatic» → paste the PAC script URL: <1>http://{{ip}}:{{port}}/proxy.pac</1>.
connect.ios4: Important: the iOS system proxy applies to Safari and some apps. HTTPS interception requires an installed and trusted CA. Apps using certificate pinning will not work through MITM. SOCKS5 cannot be set system-wide — use apps that support SOCKS5.
connect.and1: Install the CA certificate: download <1>ca.crt</1>. Then Settings → Security → Encryption & credentials → «Install certificate» → «CA certificate». (On Android 10+ you may need «User certificates» in security settings.)
connect.and2: Wi-Fi proxy: long-press the connected network → «Modify network» → «Advanced» → Proxy: «Manual» → Hostname: <1>{{ip}}</1>, port: <2>{{port}}</2>.
connect.and3: Important: Android applies the HTTP proxy only to the browser and some apps. HTTPS interception requires an installed CA. Apps using certificate pinning will not work through MITM.
connect.and4: SOCKS5 (if you need a tunnel) — in apps that support SOCKS5, specify <1>{{ip}}</1>.
connect.andWarn: If the device and the server are on different subnets, make sure ports {{ports}} are open in the firewall and use address {{ip}}.
connect.checkIntro: After configuring the proxy, run this from another device:
connect.checkHint: Two requests in a row: the first is MISS, the second is HIT. That means the cache is working.

ca.title: CA Certificate
ca.warn: HTTPS MITM interception is an explicit operator action. RustCache issues forged certificates for visited sites, signed by this root CA. Trust this CA only on machines where you intentionally run the proxy.
ca.stepDownload: Download the <1>ca.crt</1> file using the button below.
ca.stepFirefox: <1>Firefox:</1> Settings → Privacy → Certificates → Import ca.crt and check «Trust this CA to identify websites».
ca.stepChrome: <1>Chrome / system trust:</1> use the system store (see above).
ca.stepCurl: For <1>curl</1> you can pass <2>--cacert ca.crt</2> without installing into the trust store.
ca.fingerprintHint: Verify the fingerprint before installing trust:
